description: Backend: persist drawn labels for an order. Add a LabelBoxIn Pydantic schema and a new additive endpoint PUT /orders/{order_id}/labels that replaces the order's stored Detection rows with the posted boxes (delete-then-insert, same pattern as yolo.py::detect_order_images), writes an ActivityLog entry, and returns the updated OrderOut with fresh detections. Independent of the frontend; must land first because FEAT-002 calls this endpoint. Coordinates are NORMALIZED 0..1 (frontend converts px<->norm).
steps: In backend/schemas.py, after the Detection section (DetectionBox/DetectionOut), add a Pydantic v2 model: class LabelBoxIn(BaseModel) with fields label: str; confidence: float = 1.0; x: float; y: float; width: float; height: float; image_path: str = "". Match the aligned-colon style of the surrounding schemas. Add a short comment that x/y/width/height are NORMALIZED 0..1.
In backend/models/schemas.py, add LabelBoxIn to the `from schemas import (...)` import list and to __all__ (place next to DetectionBox/DetectionOut).
In backend/models/__init__.py, add LabelBoxIn to the `from .schemas import (...)` block (near DetectionBox/DetectionOut) and to the __all__ list.
In backend/routers/orders.py, add LabelBoxIn to the existing `from schemas import ...` line (keep alphabetical/grouped style).

In backend/routers/orders.py, add below get_detections a new endpoint: @router.put("/{order_id}/labels", response_model=OrderOut) def replace_labels(order_id: str, body: List[LabelBoxIn], db: Session = Depends(get_db), current: User = Depends(get_current_user)). Behavior: fetch order by Order.order_id (raise 404 'Order not found' if missing); delete existing detections with db.query(Detection).filter(Detection.order_id_fk == order.id).delete() then db.commit(); for each b in body add Detection(order_id_fk=order.id, image_path=b.image_path or "", label=b.label, confidence=b.confidence, x=b.x, y=b.y, width=b.width, height=b.height); db.commit(); db.refresh(order); call _log(db, current.name, f"Saved {len(body)} labels for order {order_id}", order_id, "success"); return order. Write a docstring stating the NORMALIZED 0..1 coordinate contract and that the frontend converts pixel<->normalized.
acceptance_criteria: `cd backend && python -c 'import main'` exits 0 (new schema imports and endpoint mount without error).
`cd backend && python -c 'from models import LabelBoxIn; from models.schemas import LabelBoxIn'` exits 0.
With the server running and a valid JWT, PUT /orders/<id>/labels with a JSON list of normalized boxes returns 200 and an OrderOut whose detections match the posted boxes.
A second PUT to the same order with a different list REPLACES the detections (count equals the new list, not the sum).
GET /orders/<id>/detections returns the boxes just saved, and GET /orders/activity contains a 'Saved N labels for order <id>' entry with severity success.
The endpoint requires auth (missing/invalid Bearer token yields 401) and returns 404 for an unknown order_id.
No existing router (auth, uploads, yolo) or endpoint behavior is changed; the only additions are LabelBoxIn and the one PUT endpoint plus re-exports.
verification: cd /Users/irfan/Downloads/DashBoard-GenAI-master/backend && python -c 'from models import LabelBoxIn; from models.schemas import LabelBoxIn'

Start uvicorn main:app --port 8000 from backend/; obtain a token via POST /auth/login (register a user with POST /auth/register if none seeded); ensure an order exists (POST /orders if needed); then: curl -X PUT localhost:8000/orders/<id>/labels -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '[{"label":"Car","x":0.1,"y":0.1,"width":0.2,"height":0.3}]' (expect 200 + OrderOut with that detection); repeat with a two-item list and confirm GET /orders/<id>/detections now returns exactly two; confirm GET /orders/activity shows the 'Saved N labels' entry.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. For FEAT-002 (frontend) integration:

ENDPOINT: PUT /orders/{order_id}/labels  (order_id is the string Order.order_id, e.g. 'ORD-1', NOT the numeric PK). Mounted under the /orders router (prefix handled in main.py; call it at `${environment.apiUrl}/orders/${orderId}/labels`).

AUTH: requires Bearer JWT via get_current_user (same dep as other /orders routes). Missing/invalid token -> 401. Use the auth.getToken() + 'Authorization: Bearer <t>' header pattern (see detection.service.ts).

REQUEST BODY: a JSON ARRAY (not an object) of LabelBoxIn. Each item: { label: string, confidence?: number (default 1.0), x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, image_path?: string (default '') }. x/y/width/height are NORMALIZED 0..1 — frontend MUST convert pixel->normalized (divide by live canvas width/height) before PUT, and normalized->pixel (multiply) when loading, guarding non-finite values (mirror runDetection() in labeling.component.ts). Send Content-Type: application/json. An empty array [] is valid and clears all labels for the order.

RESPONSE: 200 with an OrderOut object (NOT a bare detection list). Shape: { id, order_id, order_type, order_status, comment, label, accuracy, image_urls, user_id, created_at, updated_at, detections: DetectionOut[] }. detections reflects exactly what was just posted. DetectionOut item: { label, confidence, x, y, width, height, id, image_path, created_at } — note it carries x/y/width/height NORMALIZED plus server-assigned id/image_path/created_at.

SEMANTICS: delete-then-insert (REPLACE). A second PUT fully replaces prior detections (count == new list length, never the sum). Writes an ActivityLog row 'Saved N labels for order <order_id>' with severity 'success' (visible via GET /orders/activity). GET /orders/{order_id}/detections returns the saved boxes. Unknown order_id -> 404 {detail:'Order not found'}.

FIELD NUANCES: body is a top-level array; `confidence` defaults to 1.0 for manually-drawn boxes (omit it when drawing by hand); `image_path` is optional (defaults to '') — pass the order's image path if you want detections tied to a specific image, otherwise leave blank.

VERIFICATION DONE: both import checks exit 0 (`python -c 'import main'` and `python -c 'from models import LabelBoxIn; from models.schemas import LabelBoxIn'`). Full end-to-end flow verified via FastAPI TestClient against an isolated temp SQLite DB (register/login/create-order/PUT one box/PUT two boxes-replaces/GET detections/GET activity + no-token 401 + unknown-order 404): all 12 assertions passed.

ENV LIMITATION (does NOT affect this endpoint, flagged for FEAT-002 live testing): routers/auth.py encodes the JWT `sub` claim as an INTEGER (user.id). The pinned python-jose==3.3.0 rejects a non-string `sub` on decode, so a real login token is refused by get_current_user (401) when exercising via live uvicorn/curl. This is a pre-existing auth-router quirk, OUT OF SCOPE here (FEAT-001 must not touch auth). I verified my endpoint by overriding the get_current_user dependency in the test harness. If live curl testing is needed later, either (a) cast `sub` to str in create_token/get_current_user, or (b) use TestClient with a dependency override. Local Python is 3.9.6; deps are NOT installed in the repo (I used a throwaway venv, since removed).
